pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #10 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the plural of the English word loaf? (1 mark)
   A. loaves
   B. loafs
   C. loaf
   D. loafes

2. What is polite when you collect a song from an elder? (1 mark)
   A. Take the song without asking
   B. Greet them and thank them at the end
   C. Refuse to listen
   D. Interrupt while they sing

3. In the passage: Ugali is made from maize flour, what is ugali made from? (1 mark)
   A. wheat only
   B. maize flour
   C. rice
   D. millet

4. How can flashcards help with vocabulary? (1 mark)
   A. They let you practise a word and its meaning again and again
   B. They replace reading
   C. They make words disappear
   D. They cost a lot

5. What should you leave between two words? (1 mark)
   A. No space
   B. A picture
   C. A whole line
   D. A finger space

6. Tall letters such as b and d usually reach (1 mark)
   A. the bottom of the page
   B. below the base line
   C. the edge of the desk
   D. the top line

7. What is a good response when you did not understand an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Guess quietly
   B. Leave
   C. Do anything
   D. Politely ask the speaker to repeat it

8. A verb is (1 mark)
   A. a word that shows an action
   B. a word that names a person
   C. a word that describes a colour
   D. a joining word

9. Fluent reading needs (1 mark)
   A. only speed
   B. only loudness
   C. only a quiet voice
   D. smooth pace, correct words and good expression

10. In English, what usually happens to the voice at the end of a question? (1 mark)
   A. It falls to silence
   B. It stays exactly the same always
   C. It becomes a whisper
   D. It rises

11. Where should commas go in: We planted maize beans peas and kale? (1 mark)
   A. After maize and beans
   B. After planted
   C. After kale
   D. After We

12. Which of these must always begin with a capital letter in English? (1 mark)
   A. The names of colours
   B. The names of foods
   C. The names of weather
   D. The names of people

13. Which question word asks for a reason? (1 mark)
   A. Where
   B. Who
   C. Why
   D. When

14. Which habit helps you listen well? (1 mark)
   A. Looking at the floor
   B. Talking to a neighbour
   C. Sitting where you can see and hear the speaker
   D. Playing with a pencil

15. What does inferring meaning mean? (1 mark)
   A. Spelling backwards
   B. Ignoring the word
   C. Working out meaning from clues
   D. Copying words

16. Which is the best first step to find the meaning of a new word in a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Ask nobody
   B. Tear the page
   C. Skip the whole page
   D. Read the words around it for clues

17. What is a cue in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. A full stop
   B. A title
   C. A drawing
   D. The last words of the person before you

18. In a written dialogue the speaker's name usually comes (1 mark)
   A. on a different page
   B. at the start of the line
   C. in the middle of a word
   D. at the end

19. What is a sequence? (1 mark)
   A. A group of animals
   B. The order in which things happen
   C. A kind of poem
   D. A type of word

20. Which sentence belongs to the main idea Fire is dangerous? (1 mark)
   A. Maize is tasty.
   B. Never play with matches.
   C. The market is far.
   D. Rain is wet.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Give two reasons why we read fluently. (2 marks)

22. Explain how to take part in a class handwriting gallery walk. (4 marks)

23. Read: Fire can be dangerous. Never play with matches. Ask an adult to light the stove. If your clothes catch fire, stop, drop and roll. State the main idea and list three details. (5 marks)

24. List the verbs in: Otieno touched the handle and the water splashed. (3 marks)

25. Write the verbs in this instruction: Close the door and sit down. (2 marks)

26. Write a four-sentence paragraph on washing hands. Use first, next, then and finally. (4 marks)

27. Complete each sentence with a suitable verb: (a) We ______ our hands before eating. (b) Please ______ the door. (3 marks)

28. Describe three rules for writing tidily on lined paper. (3 marks)

29. Describe how a class can collect and keep cultural songs from the community. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #10 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — loaves
   Loaf changes f to ves in the plural.

2. B — Greet them and thank them at the end
   Good manners include greeting, listening and thanking.

3. B — maize flour
   The passage states that ugali is made from maize flour.

4. A — They let you practise a word and its meaning again and again
   Flashcards are a simple tool for revision.

5. D — A finger space
   A finger width keeps words clear.

6. D — the top line
   Tall letters go up to the top line.

7. D — Politely ask the speaker to repeat it
   Polite questions help you understand.

8. A — a word that shows an action
   Verbs show what is done.

9. D — smooth pace, correct words and good expression
   These are the parts of fluency.

10. D — It rises
   Many questions end with a rising voice.

11. A — After maize and beans
   The list is maize, beans, peas and kale.

12. D — The names of people
   Names of people and places begin with capital letters.

13. C — Why
   Why asks the reason.

14. C — Sitting where you can see and hear the speaker
   You can follow better when you see and hear clearly.

15. C — Working out meaning from clues
   Inferring uses clues in the context.

16. D — Read the words around it for clues
   Context clues are the words nearby.

17. D — The last words of the person before you
   You come in when you hear your cue.

18. B — at the start of the line
   The name shows who speaks.

19. B — The order in which things happen
   Sequence means order.

20. B — Never play with matches.
   It is a detail about fire safety.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps listeners understand and enjoy, and it helps the reader to understand the text.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each reason.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Write your best sentence on a strip. Display it on the wall. Walk quietly, look at each strip, and leave a kind and helpful comment.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

23. (5 marks)
   Answer: Main idea: Fire is dangerous and needs care. Details: never play with matches, ask an adult to light the stove, stop drop and roll.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the main idea and one mark for each of three details.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: touched, splashed
   Working / marking points: One mark for each verb and one mark for ignoring the nouns.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: close, sit
   Working / marking points: One mark for each verb.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: First, wet your hands. Next, rub soap on them. Then rinse them. Finally, dry them with a clean cloth.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct step in order and sequence word.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: wash (or clean) and close (or shut)
   Working / marking points: One mark for each suitable verb and one mark for correct spelling.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Letters sit on the base line, tall letters reach the top line, keep a finger space between words, and start on the left.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule, up to three.

29. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ask elders politely, listen carefully, write or record the song with permission, note the name of the person who shared it and the date, and store it in a class portfolio.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct steps.
